articles.body: Former Wimbledon champion Angela Mortimer Barrett left £676,887 ($911K) in cash and assets in her will, with the entire estate passing to her husband, celebrated tennis commentator and historian John Barrett. The amount was later reduced to £667,672 ($907K) after costs and taxes.Mortimer Barrett, who died aged 93 in August last year after a battle with cancer, was one of the leading British tennis players of her generation. She won three Grand Slam singles titles and one Grand Slam doubles title during a remarkable career.Angela Mortimer Barrett’s estate passed to husband John BarrettDocuments seen by The Sun show that Angela Mortimer Barrett’s estate was valued at £676,887 before costs and taxes. After those deductions, the amount stood at £667,672.Her will was signed in 2023. It was approved by the High Court this year.The former world No. 1 left all her cash and assets to her husband John Barrett. The couple married in 1967 and remained together until Angela’s death.Both Angela and John were later inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame. Their achievement made them only the second married couple to receive the honour, following Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi.Mortimer enjoyed a hugely successful career on the court. Her first Grand Slam singles triumph came at the French Open in Paris in 1955.She later won the Australian Open in 1958. Her biggest British success came at Wimbledon in 1961.Mortimer defeated fellow Brit Christine Truman in three sets in the Wimbledon final on Centre Court. Her victory made her the first British women’s singles champion at Wimbledon since Dorothy Round’s success in 1937.She also won the Wimbledon women’s doubles title in 1955. She partnered Anne Shilcock in the final. They defeated fellow Britons Shirley Bloomer and Patricia Ward Hales 7-5 6-1.Mortimer also reached two further Grand Slam singles finals. She lost both to American great Althea Gibson. The first defeat came at the French Open in 1956. The second followed at Wimbledon in 1958.Her career was also affected by serious illness. Mortimer was diagnosed with Entamoebic Dysentery. She underwent a three-week starvation diet as part of her recovery. The illness caused her to lose a significant amount of weight. It also left her extremely weak.After retiring from regular competition, Mortimer continued to contribute to British tennis. She served as Great Britain’s Wightman Cup captain from 1964 to 1970.She led Britain to victory in the competition in 1968.Mortimer was awarded an MBE in 1967 for her services to tennis. In 1993, she was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.A sculpture bust of Mortimer also stands outside Wimbledon’s Centre Court. It commemorates her historic 1961 triumph.Her death was announced last year by the All England Club.Mortimer and John Barrett had two children, Michael and Sarah Jane. articles.standfirst: El murciano se inspira en la Arthur Ashe, la cancha de tenis más grande del mundo
articles.summary: El murciano se inspira en la Arthur Ashe, la cancha de tenis más grande del mundo
articles.body: Nueva York es una de las capitales del mundo y, como tal, un escenario en el que cualquier cosa da la vuelta al mundo. Carlos Alcaraz regresó el pasado lunes a la competición oficial en la ciudad de los rascacielos después de un parón de 139 días por una lesión en la muñeca. “No podía haber elegido volver en un torneo mejor, aquí en el US Open, aquí en Nueva York. Es un lugar muy especial para mí”, reconocía. No en vano fue allí donde ganó el primero de sus siete títulos del Grand Slam, en 2022, convirtiéndose en el número uno más joven de la historia. Celebró la primera victoria ante Roman Safiullin sacándose la zapatilla y simulando una llamada de teléfono. En su banquillo estaba como invitado especial el rapero Travis Scott. El miércoles, en plena noche neoyorquina y con todos los focos de la Arthur Ashe sobre él tras remontar a Jaime Faria (4-6, 6-0, 6-3 y 6-2), simuló ser un arquero que lanzaba una flecha en dirección a sus allegados . “Mis hermanos me dijeron que si ganaba hiciera lo del arco y la flecha”, cuenta. El pase a la tercera ronda tenía dedicatoria especial para los pequeños de la familia Alcaraz, Sergio y Jaime. Estos le respondieron con el mismo gesto entre carcajadas. Las celebraciones de Carlitos en la central más grande del planeta tenis se han convertido en una costumbre que va ligada al espectáculo que ofrece en cada una de sus actuaciones. La pasada campaña se acordó de los golfistas Rory McIlroy y Sergio García simulando un swing de golf. El problema en la muñeca no le permitirá volver a los campos para mejor su hándicap durante un tiempo indefinido. El contraste es evidente en el 'look': del pelo rapado de la pasada edición a jugar con una media melena que tiene que sujetarse con una diadema.

articles.title: Naomi Osaka Wears Custom Thom Browne Outfit in Trending Video From 2026 US Open
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka is one of the best tennis players in the world, but her walk-on appearances have become almost as much appointment viewing as her play on the court.
articles.body:
Naomi Osaka is one of the best tennis players in the world, but her walk-on appearances have become almost as much appointment viewing as her play on the court.

Osaka donned a Thom Browne look ahead of her second-round match against Katerina Siniakova on Thursday in the U.S. Open. As ESPN's Malika Andrews noted, Osaka has featured American designers for the stateside major:

This comes after Osaka honored NBA legend Allen Iverson ahead of her first-round matchup against Anastasia Zakharova. She wore a shooting sleeve, headband and elbow pad much like Iverson used to wear on the court.

She even caught the attention of the Answer himself, who wrote on Instagram , "Wow, what a honor!! BIG FAN can't wait to meet you."

Osaka is seeded 13th in the women's singles draw of this year's tournament, although that first-round matchup against Zakharova ended up being more of a challenge than perhaps some expected.

She advanced as the favorite in straight sets, but it took two tiebreakers to finally put away the challenger.

If Osaka can advance past Siniakova on Thursday, she may have a more challenging third-round showdown with the 23rd-seeded Elise Mertens waiting if the latter can also win her second-round matchup against Maria Timofeeva.

That would give fans another opportunity to see Osaka take the court with what will surely be another notable outfit.

articles.title: US Open: Naomi Osaka urges social media influencers in attendance to respect tennis 'etiquette' after second-round win
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka opts for more understated, all-white entrance outfit ahead of her 6-2 5-7 6-1 win over Katerina Siniakova; men's third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime suffers shock exit; watch US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, on NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
The issue has become a talking point at the tournament following Osaka's opening win over Anastasia Zakharova on Monday, in which viral videos have since surfaced of some influencers not paying attention to the tennis.

After overcoming a mid-match wobble to beat Katerina Siniakova 6-2 5-7 6-1 and reach the third round in New York, Osaka said on the issue: "I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport.

"I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette.

"I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like [my] first-round match.

"Overall, I think there is huge positives. You want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette."

Osaka added: "I was going to say, today, the umpire told everyone to be quiet - more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet.

"I do think that in my first match, I wasn't really paying attention. I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was people shouting and stuff, and you could hear it quite clearly. I think it bothered my opponent, too."

Osaka wears more understated outfit for second round

Against Siniakova, it wasn't quite as headline-grabbing a display - both on and off the court - from Osaka, who sported a more understated entrance outift, for which she is gaining increasing notoriety.

The two-time US Open champion had turned heads when wearing a long, white skirt and hooded robe featuring newspaper clippings about her ahead of her tournament opener on Monday night.

But on this occasion, Osaka opted for a more understated, shimmery all-white number which wouldn't have looked out of place at Wimbledon rather than Flushing Meadows.

The 13th seed was swiftly into her stride in the first set, breaking Siniakova to love in the fourth game of the opener, which she clinched with a second break of the Czech.

Osaka appeared to be cruising to victory in the second when breaking for 4-2 and 5-3 leads, only for her serve to desert her at that time as she was broken three times in a row to ultimately drop the set 7-5.

The four-time Gland Slam winner found her footing again for the decider, dropping only one game to clinch her spot in the next round.

Swiatek storms into third round in 71 minutes

Iga Swiatek also stormed into the third round of the US Open, with a clinical 6-3 6-2 win over Nadia Podoroska that took just 71 minutes.

It was only the second meeting between the pair - the previous coming in the semi-finals of the 2020 French Open, with Swiatek victorious en route to claiming the first of her six Grand Slam titles.

The 2022 US Open champion, seeded eighth this year in New York, was back to her ruthless best.

She broke in the fourth game of the opening set and pushed on to take it 6-3, before snatching a crucial break of serve in the first game of the second set to ensure that she stayed firmly in control.

Podoroska showed some glimpses of her best form, but Swiatek was rarely under pressure and converted her first match point to book her place in the third round at Flushing Meadows for the seventh-straight time.

Auger-Aliassime becomes highest seed to fall

Men's third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime became the highest seed to be knocked out of the US Open so far when suffering a shock second-round exit to unseeded Karen Khachanov.

Khachanov, who reached the semi-final stage in New York in 2022, broke ​Auger-Aliassime's serve seven times on Louis Armstrong Stadium ‌and saved seven of the nine break points he faced en route to securing only his ​second top-10 win at a Grand Slam.

The first set was tight, with neither player giving the other any opportunities, but while Auger-Aliassime - a two-time US Open semi-finalist, including last year - edged it in the tie-break, the Canadian was unable to build on that momentum and won just seven further games.

Khachanov, who lost the opening match ‌in his three tournament tune-up events, produced some of his best tennis to reach the third round in impressive style.

The world No 50 will next face either Frenchman Benjamin Bonzi or Peruvian ‌32nd seed Ignacio Buse.

articles.title: US Open: Carlos Alcaraz planning more breaks in 'impossible' tennis schedule after more than four months out with a wrist injury
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz plans to take more ‌breaks from the tour and warned that the packed tennis calendar is contributing to injuries and ‌fatigue among players; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
The Spaniard, who returned to action after ​a lengthy layoff due to a wrist injury sustained in April to defend his US Open title, said the demands of the schedule made ​it impossible for players to compete in every major ‌event without risking burnout.

The Spaniard pointed to the absences of other top stars as evidence that the schedule is too demanding and will keep causing injuries.

World No 1 Jannik Sinner and British star Jack Draper are notable absentees at Flushing Meadows along with Holger Rune, Joao Fonseca and a host of other players.

"I took more (time off) than I wanted, to be honest, but you know, seeing how tight the calendar is, obviously I don't want to have this break because (of) an injury," said Alcaraz after coming from a set down to beat Jaime Faria in the second round.

"But in the future, I'm going to take some breaks, some long breaks. Maybe not four months, but one month, two months, missing some tournaments, because it's impossible to play them all.

"I think they (are) adding more important tournaments. You know, in a way they (are) making us play. You can say 'no'. You can keep one or two.

"You can decide your calendar, but there are some Masters 1000s, some grand slams, and we've been out playing 40 weeks if we got to play every mandatory tournament that the ATP, you know, required us to play.

"So it's impossible, and we are seeing a lot of players getting injured, a lot of players getting tired. If they don't do anything about it, we are going to see even more in the future.

"But for me, taking this break because (of) an injury, it wasn't that good, but you know, what I'm going to say is I'm going to take some breaks and miss some tournaments in the future, for sure."

Murray: I understand it from the players' perspective

Speaking to Sky Sports Tennis , Jamie Murray said: "I can totally understand it from the players' perspective. The Tour is longer than it's ever been in terms of commitment and days away from home.

"These younger guys have seen how Roger [Federer] and Rafael [Nadal] have elongated their careers - how they finished their careers as well. If they want to play until they're 34, 35, 36, they will probably have to skip tournaments and that's something the Tour needs to consider.

"The Tour is catering for over hundred players and they want to be out there competing."

Alcaraz plays Chinese world No 113 Wu Yibing in round three on Friday.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka fires back at reporter for asking question about partying after US Open victory
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka fired back at a reporter during her US Open press conference after a question about brand events implied she hadn't been training.
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka was all smiles in the media center at the U.S. Open after cruising to a straight-sets victory over Polina Iatcenko on Wednesday night to punch her ticket into the third round. That is, until one media member attempted to take the focus off of tennis and put it on Sabalenka's life off the court. The World No. 1 got into a back-and-forth with a reporter after she interrupted his question about how she was feeling in the midst of the tournament after what was a busy week leading into the year's final Grand Slam. GROUP OF INFLUENCERS FORCES PAUSE DURING US OPEN MATCH WITH CRINGEWORTHY PHOTOSHOOT IN SUITE "You guys are, like, a joke. Parties, fun, like, why would you even say that?" Sabalenka asked after rolling her eyes. "Why would you even think about that? What kind of question is that? "Just because I posted, like, some activities with brands, and you think that I’ve been partying, not training?" articles.title: US Open: Felix Auger-Aliassime beaten by Karen Khachanov in second round
articles.summary: Canadian third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime is knocked out by Russian Karen Khachanov in the second round of the US Open.
articles.body:
Third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime has been knocked out by Russian Karen Khachanov in the second round of the US Open.

A two-time finalist at the tournament, the Canadian was beaten 6-7 (5-7) 6-3 6-2 6-2 by the unseeded Russian.

Auger-Aliassime managed to fend off his opponent to edge the first set in the tie-break.

However, a mixture of too many unforced errors, coupled with some brilliant winners down the line from Khachanov, sent the 26-year-old crashing out.

His exit followed that of 24-time Grand Slam champion and fourth seed Novak Djokovic in the first round.

Auger-Aliassime reached the quarter-finals of this year's Wimbledon and French Open, but withdrew from the Rogers Cup in Montreal in August with a back injury.

"Maybe he had some physical issues," said Khachanov, 30. "It's part of our sport, it's part of tennis.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Naomi Osaka overcomes blip as Iga Swiatek also progresses
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka recovers from a second-set blip to defeat Katerina Siniakova at the US Open, while fellow former champion Iga Swiatek also progresses.
articles.body:
Naomi Osaka recovered from a second-set blip to overcome Katerina Siniakova in three sets at the US Open, while fellow former champion Iga Swiatek made smooth progress in New York.

Two-time winner Osaka, who once again walked out in a stylish outfit, served for a place in the third round during the second set but lost four straight games as she squandered a 5-3 lead.

However, after leaving the court to reset, the Japanese 28-year-old overpowered top-ranked doubles player Siniakova in the decider.

Osaka's eventual 6-2 5-7 6-1 victory confirmed a meeting with Belgian 23rd seed Elise Mertens.

After Osaka walked out for her first-round match in an outfit inspired by NBA legend Allen Iverson, the four-time major winner returned to the court on Thursday wearing a white dress embroidered with tennis racquets.

The 2018 and 2020 US Open winner took a commanding first set in half an hour, and looked on course for a straightforward victory after breaking serve for a 4-2 lead in the second by the hour mark.

That marked the start of four successive breaks of serve - including Osaka failing to close out the match - and Siniakova took full advantage as the 13th seed's consistency dipped.

But Osaka, who made 20 of her 29 unforced errors in the second set, returned to her former levels and replied by winning six of the final seven games to complete victory in two hours and two minutes.

"The match was definitely really tough. I just felt like I was a little bit too hard on myself after opportunities in the second set," Osaka told the crowd inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I took the bathroom break, regrouped a little, came back and just tried to have no regrets."

With that, she became just the second Japanese woman in the Open era to record 80 Grand Slam singles wins, after Ai Sugiyama.

It is also the first time since 2018 that Osaka, who reached the semi-finals in New York 12 months ago, has reached the third round at all four Grand Slam tournaments in the same season.

"I just told myself that it's an honour to play on this court, honestly," Osaka said.

"I just want to keep playing in front of you guys if possible, so to keep fighting as best as I can.

"The energy from the crowd, it's very lively and I have the experience of growing up here and playing on this court many times. It's really fun."

Swiatek, a six-time major winner whose sole US Open triumph arrived in 2022, had no such issues.

Poland's 25-year-old former world number one defeated Argentina's Nadia Podoroska 6-3 6-2 to set up a meeting with Czech player Marie Bouzkova, who earlier ended Briton Harriet Dart's tournament.

However, American Madison Keys survived a huge scare as the former finalist saved five match points to come through a thrilling match against Hungary's Anna Bondar.

After forcing a third set, Keys, the 22nd seed at her home slam, trailed the decider by a double break of serve.

She stayed alive after Bondar produced back-to-back double faults on her first two match points, and three more on her subsequent service game, before breaking again to level the set and eventually clinching a 10-point tie-break to win 5-7 6-4 7-6 (10-5).

In the women's draw, Naomi Osaka defeated Katerina Siniakova in three sets, while Madison Keys staved off five match points to defeat Anna Bondar in a thriller.

Friday's duel is expected to be no different.

Shelton enters as the clear favorite considering his current form and momentum.

If Shapovalov can find his aggressive tennis early, he has what it takes to pull off the upsets.

However, the match could hinge on his mental fortitude and any lapses in concentration.

Shelton should be able to do just enough with the crowd behind him.

The six-time major champion won 77 percent of points on her serve while playing a stellar return game.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Harriet Dart struggles with illness in Marie Bouzkova loss
articles.summary: Britain's Harriet Dart says she felt "under the weather" as she struggles in the heat during her second-round loss to Marie Bouzkova at the US Open.
articles.body:
Britain's Harriet Dart said she felt "under the weather" as she struggled in the heat during her second-round loss to Marie Bouzkova at the US Open.

Dart struggled for rhythm in a 6-2 6-2 defeat by Czech 25th seed Bouzkova as temperatures reached around 30C in New York.

Dart's defeat means Fran Jones is the last remaining Briton in either singles draw at Flushing Meadows.

Jones faces American 14th seed Iva Jovic later on Thursday.

Dart draped ice towels around her neck and used cold-air hoses at the changeovers against Bouzkova as she attempted to cool down.

"I have been a bit under the weather. It is what it is, sadly," Dart, 30, said.

"It was quite warm. I had a temperature, I was trying to cool down. I've played many weeks in a row.

"I am not used to air conditioning being pumped everywhere. We go from really hot outside to freezing inside.

"All credit to my opponent, she is an incredibly tough player, so even if I had been at full capacity, I don't know."

Dart, who is ranked 131st in the world, struggled on serve against Bouzkova, committing eight double faults and landing only 45% of her first serves.

Bouzkova took command almost straight away, winning seven games in a row to clinch the first set and go a double break up in the second.

From there Dart was unable to recover as Bouzkova safely saw out the rest of the match to reach the third round, where she will face Polish eighth seed Iga Swiatek.

Dart's exit follows compatriot Katie Boulter's second-round defeat by Karolina Muchova in only 58 minutes on Wednesday.

In the men's draw, Jacob Fearnley and Toby Samuel lost in the second round, while Cameron Norrie, Arthur Fery, Harry Wendelken and Jan Choinski exited in the first round.

articles.title: Cristina Bucsa pasa otra ronda en el US Open y está a un triunfo de defender los octavos
articles.standfirst: La tenista cántabra ha superado este jueves a la japonesa Sakatsume en el súper 'tie break'
articles.summary: La tenista cántabra ha superado este jueves a la japonesa Sakatsume en el súper 'tie break'
articles.body: El tenis femenino español se ha asegurado una representante en la tercera ronda del US Open. Se trata de Cristina Bucsa, que ha derrotado este jueves a la japonesa Himeno Sakatsume, la 144 del mundo y procedente de la previa, por 7-6(6), 6-7(0) y 7-6(6), en el súper 'tie break'. De esta forma, la cántabra se sitúa a un solo triunfo de defender los octavos de la pasada edición, que es su mejor resultado en los torneos del Grand Slam. Los restos se impusieron a los servicios en un auténtico carrusel de 'breaks'. La lluvia de los dos últimos días en Nueva York dio paso al sol y el calor. Bucsa impuso su experiencia y su mejor ranking, a pesar del sufrimiento, para seguir vida en el cuadro individual femenino. Esta campaña dio un empujón a su trayectoria con el título del WTA 500 de Mérida. Cristina, la 40 del ranking a sus 28 años, estará muy atenta a lo que pase en el partido que abre la sesión nocturna de la Arthur Ashe entre Coco Gauff (4) y Paula Badosa. Y es la ganadora será su rival en la tercera ronda del sábado. Un duelo fratricida con Badosa aseguraría la presencia de una española en octavos.

articles.title: Nick Kyrgios cleared to return to tennis after accepting one-month ban for positive cocaine test
articles.summary: Nick Kyrgios is eligible to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive for cocaine.
articles.body:
Nick Kyrgios is eligible to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive for cocaine.

The Australian, 31, was provisionally suspended on 4 August after a sample he submitted during the Mallorca Open in June was found to contain benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

Kyrgios told investigators from the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) that he used cocaine at a nightclub in Magaluf in the early hours of 20 June.

He played his first-round match at the Mallorca tournament two days later, losing in straight sets to compatriot Adam Walton.

The ITIA accepted he used cocaine outside of competition after consulting with an an independent expert.

Kyrgios could have faced a maximum three-month ban but it has been reduced to one month after he entered a treatment programme.

His one-month ban ended on Thursday, 3 September.

Kyrgios, who has fallen to 918 in the world rankings, will also lose his prize money of 6,570 euros (£5,650).

When the positive test was announced, Kyrgios said he would step away from social media and public life for the next 28 days to "focus on getting myself right".

The former world number 13 has played just four singles matches this season, having struggled with knee and wrist injuries in recent years.

He last played in the men's doubles at Wimbledon, where he and partner Alexander Bublik lost in the first round.

After his initial suspension was announced, Kyrgios said the past few years of injuries had taken "a huge toll on me, both mentally and physically".

"My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do," he wrote in a lengthy statement on Instagram.

"Coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

Cocaine is classified as a stimulant and substance of abuse on the World Anti-Doping Agency's prohibited list.

Kyrgios has long been a controversial figure in tennis.

His behaviour on court has been widely criticised and he has been given numerous large fines for smashing racquets, making audible obscenities and arguing with the umpire.

In 2023, he admitted assaulting an ex-girlfriend two years earlier. He avoided a criminal conviction.

He was criticised further for making a series of comments which have been considered misogynistic.

In 2024 he shared a post from controversial influencer Andrew Tate. He later said he had gone "to all lengths" to distance himself from the self-proclaimed misogynist.

Kyrgios was also critical of the handling of two high-profile anti-doping cases involving top players Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek, calling them "disgusting" for tennis.

Kyrgios has won seven ATP Tour singles titles and reached the Wimbledon final in 2022, losing in four sets to Novak Djokovic.

He and compatriot Thanasi Kokkinakis won the Australian Open men's doubles title together in 2022.

Kyrgios has also spoken about his struggles with mental health, saying he "genuinely contemplated" suicide and spent time in a psychiatric hospital in London after losing at Wimbledon in 2019.

articles.title: Nick Kyrgios Accepts a One-Month Suspension for Testing Positive for Cocaine
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — Nick Kyrgios accepted a one-month suspension from the International Tennis Integrity Association for testing positive for cocaine at a tournament in Spain in June, the organization announced Thursday.
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — Nick Kyrgios accepted a one-month suspension from the International Tennis Integrity Association for testing positive for cocaine at a tournament in Spain in June, the organization announced Thursday.

The 31-year-old from Australia had been provisionally suspended since Aug. 4, which was revealed just over two weeks later.

The ITIA in its announcement said Kyrgios told investigators that he socially used cocaine during a night out before he was due to play in Mallorca, and after consulting with an expert from the World Anti-Doping Association, accepted that it was outside of competition.

WADA's default three-month ban can be reduced to one by completing a treatment program. The ITIA said Kyrgios' suspension is over Thursday pending the completing of that program.

Kyrgios' prize money and rankings points from the Mallorca event are forfeited. He lost his only match to countryman Adam Walton.

A finalist at Wimbledon in 2022 when he lost to Novak Djokovic , Kyrgios has played only four ATP singles matches this year and is ranked 918th in the world.
